title: Towards an Expressivity-Normalized Energy-Demand Comparison of ANNs and SNNs
abstract: arXiv:2608.29869v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) are often regarded as energy-efficient alternatives to artificial neural networks (ANNs), yet their advantage depends critically on both network architecture and data properties. We develop an analytical framework to compare fully-connected ReLU ANNs and integrate-and-fire SNNs for time-series data with respect to their theoretical energy efficiency at matched expressive capacity. By relating an inference-energy model to theoretical bounds on representational expressivity, we derive an expressivity-normalized efficiency ratio and explicit thresholds in network width, spike sparsity, and ANN depth scaling. Our analysis characterizes the regimes in which event-driven computation offsets the temporal overhead of SNNs, providing capacity-aware principles for designing energy-efficient temporal networks. It shows that ANNs exceed SNNs in expressivity-normalized efficiency only in specific regimes.

translated_title: 迈向表达能力归一化的人工神经网络与脉冲神经网络能耗需求比较
translated_abstract: 脉冲神经网络（SNN）通常被视为人工神经网络（ANN）的高能效替代方案，但其优势在很大程度上取决于网络架构和数据特性。我们开发了一个分析框架，用于在表达能力匹配的条件下，比较全连接ReLU人工神经网络与积分发放脉冲神经网络在处理时间序列数据时的理论能效。通过将推理能耗模型与表征表达能力的理论界相关联，我们推导出了表达能力归一化的效率比率，以及网络宽度、脉冲稀疏性和ANN深度缩放方面的明确阈值。我们的分析刻画了事件驱动计算能够抵消SNN时间开销的特定区间，为设计高能效的时间网络提供了容量感知的设计原则。结果表明，只有在特定区间内，ANN的表达能力归一化效率才会超过SNN。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个表达能力归一化的理论分析框架，推导出网络宽度、脉冲稀疏性和ANN深度缩放的明确阈值条件，从而刻画了ANN与SNN在时间序列任务上各自能效占优的具体区间。
en_tdlr: This paper develops an expressivity-normalized analytical framework that derives explicit thresholds in network width, spike sparsity, and ANN depth scaling, characterizing the specific regimes in which ANNs or SNNs achieve superior theoretical energy efficiency for time-series tasks.
